verses.text: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
"How long will you talk like this? Your words are blowing like a strong wind.
Does God twist justice? Does the Almighty distort what is right?
If your children sinned against him, he handed them over to the consequences of their disobedience.
If you'll seek God earnestly, plead with the Almighty.
If you're pure and upright, he'll surely rise to help you and restore your home to prosperity.
Even if your beginnings were small, your future would be far greater.
Ask the generations who came before us. Find out what their ancestors learned.
We only arrived yesterday and know so little, because our days on earth are a passing shadow.
Won't they teach you and speak to you from what they've learned in their hearts?
Can papyrus grow without a marsh? Can reeds grow without water?
While still green and uncut, they wither faster than any other reed.
That's what happens to everyone who forgets God. The hope of the godless dies away.
Their confidence snaps. What they trust is as fragile as a spider's web.
They lean on their house, but it won't stand. They grab hold of it, but it won't last.
They're like a plant green in the sun, with shoots spreading across the garden.
Its roots wrap around a pile of stones and reach into the rocky ground.
If it's torn out of its place, that place disowns it and says, 'I've never seen you.'
That's all the joy it gets from its course. Other plants spring from the ground in its place.
God won't reject a blameless person, and he won't lend a hand to those who do wrong.
He'll yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy.
Those who hate you will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will disappear."
